# Conditional algorithm consequence catalog

Data date: 2026-10-28

> **Conditional catalog; see each entry's review status.** Unreviewed entries are drafts; an AI audit is recorded separately from a human review. The bounds depend on the named SAT assumptions. Schema validation and reproducible rendering are mechanical checks, not mathematical proof verification or a certification of the underlying result.

[日本語](CATALOG.ja.md) · [FPT](FPT.md) · [Exact algorithms](EXACT.md) · [Assumptions and sources](ASSUMPTIONS.md) · [Candidates](CANDIDATES.md)

The FPT track measures the parameter dependence; the exact-algorithm track measures dependence on the stated input-size quantity. Decision, counting, optimization, and search variants are distinguished on the entry pages. Fixed constants remain independent of the parameter and input length. Inclusion alone is not a claim of novelty or a best-known bound.

The conditional running time is the listed factor multiplied by $L^{O(1)}$, where $L$ is the original input length. Substitute the declared parameter or size measure for $x$. Detailed measure definitions, restrictions, and encoding sizes are given on each problem's page.

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(x) &= 2^{O(x\log\log x/\sqrt{\log x})}, \\
B(x) &= 2^{O(x/\sqrt{\log x})}.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Comparison status:** entries not listed below have not been systematically compared with known algorithms. Recorded assessments:

- [Counting Perfect Matchings](docs/en/exact-count-perfect-matchings.md): `classical-benchmark-only` — For the bipartite 0–1 case, Ryser’s formula is a classical $2^t\operatorname{poly}(t)$ bit-time benchmark for t×t matrices. The new guarantee B(m) is subexponential in t when m=O(t), but the substitution m=Θ(t²) gives no improvement over that benchmark. This is not a claim about the latest best bound.

## Alternative reported-formalization bound

Each entry also explicitly depends on `sat26-reported-formal` for the separate, weaker bound below, with its own measure substituted for $x$. The paper bound and this bound are alternatives under their respective assumptions; the reported formalization is not independently checked by this repository.

$$
2^{O(x(\log\log x)^2/\sqrt{\log x})}L^{O(1)}
$$
